title: `Timer` that ticks on physics and ignores timescale is wrong
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:

- `4.5.dev5`
- `4.4.1`.

Can't test on `4.4`, because `ignore_time_scale` does not exist in that version.

### System information

Godot v4.5.dev5 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7216) - AMD Ryzen 7 3800X 8-Core Processor (16 threads)

### Issue description

When `process_callback` is set to `physics`, and `ignore_time_scale` is `true`, if `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second` is set to anything other than `60`, the timer go slower or faster than it should.

### Steps to reproduce

Here is how the attached project reproduces the issue:

- One label accumulates `delta` in `_process()` to measure time.
- Another label uses a `Timer` which triggers a signal once per second to increment the label.
   - The `Timer` has `process_callback` is set to `physics`, and `ignore_time_scale` is `true`.
- `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second` is set to `50` instead of `60` which is the default.

When you play the project, you'll see two labels in the top left of the screen. The first one is the `delta`-based timer, the second one is that `Timer`-based timer.

The `delta`-based timer:

```gdscript
extends Label

var time: float

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	time += delta
	text = "%d" % time
```

The `Timer`-based timer:

```gdscript
extends Label

func _on_timer_timeout() -> void:
	text = "%d" % (text as int + 1)
```
